claims: C1 the assistant might cause harm by simply following user or developer instructions
C2 harmful-instruction situations involve a direct conflict between empowering the user and preventing harm
C3 the model should obey user and developer instructions except when they fall into specific categories that require refusal or safe completion

concepts.name: risk_taxonomy
concepts.gloss: R is one of the three categories of AI risk: misaligned goals, execution errors, or harmful instructions; each has distinct mitigations

concepts.name: harmful_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is a user or developer instruction whose simple following would cause harm, such as providing self-harm instructions or advice that helps the user carry out a violent act

concepts.name: user_or_developer_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction given by a user or by a developer

concepts.name: empowerment_harm_conflict
concepts.gloss: I is a situation in which empowering the user by following the instruction directly conflicts with preventing the harm the instruction would cause

concepts.name: prohibited_category
concepts.gloss: C is one of the specific categories of instructions that require refusal or safe completion rather than obedience
concepts.inference: the clause says instructions fall into 'specific categories' that require refusal or safe completion, but does not enumerate them; the categories are established by the cross-referenced stay_in_bounds clause

concepts.name: instruction_in_category
concepts.gloss: instruction I falls into prohibited category C
concepts.inference: the clause speaks of instructions falling into specific categories, so a relation between an instruction and a category must exist

concepts.name: requires_refusal
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction that falls into a category requiring refusal
concepts.inference: the clause says some categories 'require refusal', so an instruction in such a category requires refusal

concepts.name: requires_safe_completion
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction that falls into a category requiring safe completion
concepts.inference: the clause says some categories require 'safe completion', so an instruction in such a category requires safe completion

ontology.gloss: I is a harmful instruction: a user or developer instruction whose simple following would cause harm
I is a harmful-instruction situation that directly conflicts empowering the user with preventing harm

ontology.inference: the clause says instructions fall into 'specific categories' that require refusal or safe completion, but does not enumerate them; the categories are established by the cross-referenced stay_in_bounds clause
ontology.gloss: I is an instruction that falls into a category requiring refusal

ontology.inference: the clause says instructions fall into 'specific categories' that require refusal or safe completion, but does not enumerate them; the categories are established by the cross-referenced stay_in_bounds clause
ontology.gloss: I is an instruction that falls into a category requiring safe completion

asserts.read_back: following instruction % is forbidden when % is a harmful instruction that falls into a category requiring refusal
following instruction % is forbidden when % is a harmful instruction that falls into a category requiring safe completion
refusing instruction % is permitted when % is a harmful instruction that falls into a category requiring refusal
completing instruction % safely is permitted when % is a harmful instruction that falls into a category requiring safe completion

closure.reason: the clause says the model should obey user and developer instructions except when they fall into specific categories requiring refusal or safe completion; the exception is the only permitted deviation, so silence about other deviations prohibits them
the clause permits refusal only for instructions in categories that require refusal; it does not prohibit refusal in other situations, so silence leaves it permitted
the clause permits safe completion only for instructions in categories that require safe completion; it does not prohibit safe completion in other situations, so silence leaves it permitted
